stem: A 6-year-old is prescribed montelukast for chronic asthma management; what daily dose is appropriate for this age group?
explanation: Montelukast 5 mg once daily is the correct dose for children aged 6 years and older.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Montelukast dosing is age-based, and the 6-year-old age group is given 5 mg once daily.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because 2 mg once daily is not the listed asthma dose for this age group.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 4 mg once daily is used for younger children aged 2 to 5 years.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because children aged 6 years and older receive montelukast 5 mg once daily.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 10 mg once daily is not the recommended paediatric dose in this context.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because montelukast is prescribed once daily, not twice daily.
